authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Curated UI, §§1–5 (widget schema, β, compose(r), salience, knapsack); Cowan 2001 (K ≈ 4); Hick 1952 / Hyman 1953 (choice cost); measured against the Slice-13 Python implementation in sustena/core/curated_ui.py
note: ★★ The Rust build of what Slice 13 shipped in Python, so this row has a **reference implementation to measure against** rather than only a spec. The algorithm is at parity on purpose; the sharpenings are three, and each closes a gaming surface the reference left open.

★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★_1_there_is_NO_EventClass_in_this_core_: ★★ Checked first, because β's key depends on it. `EventClass` and `event_class` are **grep-0** in `sustena-core/src`; the Rust `Event` carries `name: String` and nothing that could serve as a class. ★ And the reference's `event_class` is **also just a string** — `WidgetSchema.binding_key` returns either that string or a `UNIT` sentinel, both used as plain `dict` keys. So there was no type to port, and inventing an `EventClass` taxonomy would have been this core deciding how the reference should have named its events. β keys on `Event.name` directly.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★_2_the_one_sharpening_that_IS_worth_it: ★★ `BindingKey::{Unit, Event(String)}` makes `EventClass ∪ Unit` genuinely the ∪ the notation claims, rather than a magic string sharing a namespace with real event names. ★ Two effects, and the second is the useful one: the sentinel collision disappears (**theoretical** — nobody names an event `__unit__`, and it is worth saying that rather than dressing it up), and a widget with **no** binding becomes **unrepresentable** — which the reference has to reject at runtime with *'must declare either event_class or unit=true'*.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★_3_UI_2's_typed_population_is_exactly_: `BindingTable::build` and `compose_view` take a **`WidgetSet`**, not a list of declarations — so every widget in β has already type-checked against `dim(S)` and `T`. **A widget with a made-up input cannot enter the knapsack**, because it never loaded. Doing UI-1 first would have meant a compose that ranks widgets whose inputs may not exist, and UI-2 would then have been a retrofit through it.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★_4_and_the_urgency_signal_is_ALREADY_HE: `region.rs`'s `Region::distance` returns `Distance { weighted, per_dimension, binding, relations_violated }` — the real weighted distance to `V`, with per-dimension excesses. The reference's urgency is an explicitly-declared **proxy** (`pct = spent/allocated`) and UI-7 says exactly why: *'deliberately reusing the Monitor's Slice-0 signal because CUSUM/EWMA don't exist'*. In this core they do.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★_5_UI_7_reconcile_2026_08_17_the_blind: ★★★ Checked in code before touching anything, and it holds: **`spent/allocated` does not exist in this core's urgency path.** Every `allocated` hit in `sustena-core/src` is `budget.rs`'s operator writing real state paths, a `compose.rs`/`inverse.rs` test fixture, or the one docstring in `curated.rs` *describing* the reference's proxy. `urgency_of` calls `region.distance()` and nothing else. ★★ **There is no denominator, so there is no zero-denominator case to special-case wrongly** — the `allocated <= 0 -> 0.0` artifact is structurally impossible rather than fixed. UI-1 discharged it, and the honest move for UI-7 was to **say so and narrow**, not to re-derive a proxy that is gone. ★ The reference's *'unmapped captures pinned at 1.1'* constant is likewise **grep-0** here — a Python artifact of a queue this core does not have, recorded as checked.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★_6_the_GENUINE_residual_was_the_WEIGHT: ⚠ `pub const ALPHA_URGENCY: f64 = 0.75` — **exactly the defect UI-7's row names**: *'a policy living in a module constant'*. §IV is blunt: *'Nothing derives α = 0.75. It is a declared preference ... belongs in a declared constraint where it can be **argued with**, not a module constant.'* ★ And the precedent was already in this codebase: `Region::weights`'s own docstring reads *'A modelling choice, not a fact. Declared here so it can be argued with.'* The salience weights simply had not been given that treatment. `SaliencePolicy` is it.

divergence.statement: The algorithm is the reference's and is ported at parity: `score(w) = α·urgency + λ·relevance` with `α = 0.75` / `λ = 0.25`, a real 0/1 knapsack DP over integer cost and score×1000, `K = 4`, and `(selected, excluded)` both returned score-ordered. Three things are sharper, and each closes a gaming surface rather than adding a feature: **the ∪ is a sum type**, **the population is typed** (UI-2), and **cost is derived rather than declared**.
divergence.★★★_the_sharpening_that_matters_most_COS: ★★★ The reference's `knapsack_select` docstring says the cost model is *'Hick-Hyman's superlinear per-item cost — a widget with more inputs costs more attention chunks to parse, **see WidgetSchema.cost**'*. Following that pointer: `cost: int = 1`, read straight from the spec with `int(raw.get('cost', 1))`. **The formula is written down and never computed.** That is a gaming surface of exactly the `colour_rule` kind — a widget reading eight dimensions can declare `cost: 1` and get a bargain, while an honest widget declaring `3` is penalised for its honesty. Here `attention_cost` is **derived** from `inputs.len()` — which UI-2 already checked against `dim(S)` — and superlinear: `1 + n(n−1)/2`, the pairwise relating a reader has to do. ★★ It also closes the one hole share-of-`d(s,V)` would otherwise open: a widget **could** raise its urgency by declaring more dimensions, but the same declaration raises its cost superlinearly, so **the attention budget prices the strategy out** and the greedy move loses to two focused widgets. Asserted, not argued.
divergence.★★_the_counterweight_THE_ALGORITHM_IS_TH: ★★ This row ports rather than invents, and the thing being ported is right. The reference's knapsack is a **genuine 0/1 DP** — not the sort-and-take-N that would have been easy to ship and hard to notice — with the backtrack, the integer scaling and the excluded-with-scores return all already there, which is what makes *'N other things stayed quiet'* a true statement on the phone today. ★ `α = 0.75` dominant is its choice and is the right one. ★★ And the *no second notion of important* discipline is the reference's own and was honoured under pressure: Slice 0 derived the urgency signal, and Slice 13 **reused that formula verbatim** rather than inventing a selection-specific one. This core inherits a signal that was already single, and only substitutes a better measurement of the same thing. ★ Its urgency proxy is **declared as a proxy** in its own row, with the reason — which is why replacing it is an upgrade rather than a correction.

the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.★ compose (real hits in Rust, and a DIFF: ★ `compose.rs` is OP-5's **checked composition** — `wp`, pathway chaining, illegal chains refused at write time. Real, load-bearing, and nothing to do with `compose(r)`. Named because *compose* is the first word a reviewer greps, and it lands squarely on the wrong module; the newcomer is `curated::compose_view` for that reason.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.★ Candidate (a collision, not a false po: `ooda::Candidate` is a decision option surfaced at DECIDE. Twenty-seventh collision; the newcomer took `WidgetCandidate`.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.EventClass / event_class (grep-0 on BOTH: Recorded as checked. The reference's `event_class` is a string field, not a type — so *there is an EventClass to port* would have been wrong in both directions.
the_greppable_false_positives_named_so_n.★ spent / allocated (real hits in Rust,: ★★ The grep a reviewer would run to check UI-7, and it returns hits — all of them innocent. `budget.rs` writes `finances.pockets.*.allocated` because that is the operator's job; `compose.rs`/`inverse.rs` use them in fixtures; `curated.rs` mentions `spent/allocated` **once, in prose describing the reference**. And `View.spent` is the **attention** budget, not money. Named so a non-zero count is not read as *the proxy is still here*.

divergence.the_honest_limits: ★★ `render` STAYS OPAQUE, SO THIS RANKS RATHER THAN RENDERS — the output is a scored selection with its reasons, not a view fragment. The reference's `WIDGET_RENDERERS` are hand-written per render id and belong to a surface with a display; MON-7 drew the same line for the same reason. · ★★ URGENCY IS A **SHARE** OF `d(s,V)`, WHICH IS A MODELLING CHOICE AND IS STATED — a widget's urgency is the per-dimension excess it can show over the sustain's total, so it is relative to what else is wrong. A household with one breached dimension gives the widget reading it an urgency of 1.0; the same widget in a household with three breaches reads lower without changing. That is the intended reading (*the fraction of the trouble this card can show you*) and it is named so nobody infers an absolute. · ★ `relations_violated` CONTRIBUTES NO URGENCY — `region.rs` deliberately names failing relations rather than scoring them, because a boolean has no natural distance; so a sustain whose only breach is a relation reads zero urgency here. Inherited, correct, and worth stating: the widget layer does not invent the number the region layer refused to. · ★★ A ZERO-SCORE WIDGET IS NEVER SELECTED — the DP takes an item only when it strictly improves the total. That is right rather than a gap (`K ≈ 4` is scarce, and a card worth nothing is the noise a curated surface removes) and it is **at parity** with the reference; nothing is hidden, since it returns in `excluded` with its `0.0`. · ★ `device` IS CARRIED AND NOT USED — it rides in the request and comes back in the view, and ranking does not consult it. Naming a device-specific budget would be inventing policy; a host that wants one passes a different `budget`. · ★ RELEVANCE IS TOKEN OVERLAP, NOT MEANING — the same shape the reference uses, and it is the weaker term (`λ = 0.25`) precisely because the usual question is *what needs me right now* rather than a search. · AND NOTHING CALLS `compose_view` FROM AN ENGINE — a host assembles `r` and calls it, at a surface's cadence, the same seam MON-7 draws. · ★★ **UNDECLARED IS REPORTED, NOT PENALISED** — a widget reading only unbounded dimensions gets urgency `0` and an `Undeclared` basis; it is **not** given a floor, a boost, or a warning severity. Ranking it up would be this core deciding the household should care about something it declined to bound, which is the fabrication the whole row is against. The surface is told; the score is not touched. · ★ **THE BASIS IS PER-WIDGET, NOT PER-DIMENSION-OF-THE-SUM** — a widget reading one bounded and one unbounded dimension reads `Undeclared`, naming the unbounded one, even though its bounded half did contribute. That is the conservative direction (it flags that the reading is incomplete) and it is stated rather than left to be inferred. · ★ **THE SUM-TO-ONE RULE IS A CONSTRAINT ON THE ARGUMENT, NOT A DERIVATION** — it makes scores comparable; it does not make `0.75` correct. Nothing here derives the ratio, and the row's point stands: it is a preference, now held somewhere it can be disagreed with.
divergence.★★_UI_7_the_blind_spot_is_the_PROXY'S_an: ★★★ The row's defect is precise and it belongs to the **proxy**: `pct = spent/allocated` is undefined at zero allocation, and the reference returns `0.0` there — so **an unfunded pocket that has been spent from scores as perfectly calm**, which is backwards. That is a manufactured zero. ★★ UI-1 replaced the proxy with `d(s,V)`, and **CASE A proves the fix rather than asserting it**: with `V` declaring the wall the pocket's spending drove state through (`balance >= 0`), the unfunded-pocket state reads a **non-zero** urgency and a `Bounded` basis. The metric the proxy was standing in for catches exactly what the proxy called calm. ★★★ **And CASE B is the finding worth carrying**: where `V` declares **no** wall on what a widget reads, `d(s,V)` is honestly `0` — but that is *the household declared nothing here*, not *nothing is wrong*. Rather than invent a wall to force urgency (which would be this core deciding what a household should care about), the basis is **reported**: `UrgencyBasis::{Bounded, Undeclared}`. Two widgets can read the same `0.0` and mean opposite things, and a surface can now say **silence** instead of showing calm. ★ The proxy manufactured a wrong zero; `d(s,V)` gives an honest zero, and this makes *which kind* legible.
divergence.★★_the_weights_are_now_DECLARED_POLICY_n: ★★ `SaliencePolicy::declared(alpha, lambda)` replaces the bare constants at the call site — the household passes it, and a **widget has nowhere to put one**, so the weights are argued with by the household and by nobody else. ★★ It **does** keep a `Default`, and that is the honest call rather than a lapse: `TrustPolicy` (IMM-10) has none because what a trust level may reach is a per-deployment decision with no safe answer, whereas here the article states a preference and it is a good one. The defect was never *there is a default* — it was *there is no way to hold a different one*. So the default survives, **named as a declaration rather than a derivation** in the constant's own docstring. ★★★ **Two things are not arguable, and they are refused**: `alpha > lambda`, because a policy letting a *search query* outrank *the household being in danger* would reintroduce at the weights exactly the gaming UI-1 closed at the inputs; and `alpha + lambda = 1`, so `score` in `[0,1]` keeps meaning the same thing across sustains and the DP's integer scaling stays interpretable. **You may argue the ratio; you may not argue urgency into second place.**

beta_cases.name: ★_beta_keys_on_an_event_class_or_Unit_never_on_an_operator
beta_cases.why: ★ β is the formal **inverse** of the operator→widget `ui_schema`, and the type says so: `BindingKey` has exactly two shapes and neither is an operator name. Asserted by looking up a real operator (`budget.allocate`) and finding nothing — not because the lookup fails, but because β has no key that could hold it.
beta_cases.expect: Unit and the event class both resolve; an operator name resolves to nothing

beta_cases.name: ★★_an_event_bound_widget_is_NOT_a_candidate_when_its_class_did_not_fire
beta_cases.why: ★★ Event-first in **behaviour**, not only in shape. Absent from the recent log means the widget is never scored at all — not scored and ranked low. This is exactly what stops `compose` degrading into *scan everything and rank*, which is the failure mode the event-first framing exists to prevent, and it is checked by `candidates_considered` rather than by the selection.

beta_cases.name: it_becomes_a_candidate_the_moment_its_class_appears
beta_cases.why: The other half, and it carries **why**: the candidate's eligibility names the class that fired. A surface can say *this is here because a pocket was spent from* rather than *this is here*.

urgency_cases.name: ★★_a_widget_reading_the_breached_dimension_outranks_one_reading_a_healthy_one
urgency_cases.why: ★★ Urgency is the real `d(s,V)`, restricted to what the widget reads. With `balance` 60 outside its band and `mood` inside, the money card carries urgency and the feelings card carries **exactly zero** — and the score ordering follows. This is the one signal the Monitor escalates on and MON-7 encodes, now with a third consumer, and no widget had a say in any of it.

urgency_cases.name: inside_the_viable_region_nothing_is_urgent
urgency_cases.why: `d(s,V) = 0` ⇒ every urgency is 0. Correct rather than degenerate: a household inside its own viable region has nothing urgent to show, and a surface that manufactured urgency there would be training people to ignore it.

urgency_cases.name: ★_a_widget_cannot_set_its_own_urgency
urgency_cases.why: ★ The only lever a widget has is **which dimensions it declares** — and those are checked against `dim(S)` at load by UI-2, so it cannot name one that does not exist. The distance itself is the household's, computed by `region.rs`. The same state read twice, breached and not, moves the urgency; nothing the widget does moves it.
urgency_cases.expect: urgency rises with the breach, not with anything the widget declares about itself

urgency_cases.name: cost_is_superlinear_in_the_declared_inputs
urgency_cases.why: `1 + n(n−1)/2` — 1, 2, 4, 7 — with the second difference asserted positive, so *superlinear* is checked rather than asserted. The justification is legible: reading `n` items is not `n` work, it is the pairwise relating between them.

urgency_cases.name: ★★★_grabbing_every_dimension_to_look_urgent_is_SELF_DEFEATING
urgency_cases.why: ★★★ The property that makes share-of-`d(s,V)` safe. A widget declaring all three dimensions captures the **whole** of the household's distance and scores maximally — and costs 4 chunks. Against a budget of 3 it is **excluded**, while two focused widgets costing 1 each are both selected. The greedy move buys the highest score at a price no budget can afford, so the attention budget prices out the gaming rather than a rule forbidding it.
urgency_cases.expect: the greedy widget excluded at cost 4; two focused widgets selected

urgency_cases.name: ★★★_the_proxy_blind_spot_is_gone_because_there_is_no_denominator
urgency_cases.why: ★★★ CASE A, and the row's own worry run as a test: a pocket with **zero allocation** that has been spent from, driving `balance` negative through a wall `V` declares. Under the proxy this is `spent/allocated` at a zero denominator, special-cased to `0.0` — *perfectly calm*, backwards. Under `d(s,V)` it reads **non-zero** with a `Bounded` basis. The metric the proxy stood in for catches exactly what the proxy called calm, and the artifact is structurally impossible here because **there is no denominator at all**.

urgency_cases.name: ★★★_an_undeclared_dimension_reads_zero_but_says_it_is_SILENCE_not_safety
urgency_cases.why: ★★★ CASE B, and the finding. Where `V` bounds nothing the widget reads, `d(s,V)` is honestly `0` — but that means *the household declared no wall here*, not *nothing is wrong*. **No wall is invented to force urgency**; instead the basis reports `Undeclared`, naming the dimension, and `describe()` says *silence rather than safety*. The proxy manufactured a wrong zero; this gives an honest one and makes which kind legible.
urgency_cases.expect: urgency = 0.0, basis = Undeclared { mood }, is_measured() = false

urgency_cases.name: ★★_an_honest_zero_inside_V_is_told_apart_from_an_unmeasured_one
urgency_cases.why: ★★ The distinction side by side: two widgets, the same `0.0`, opposite meanings. One is inside the viable region (calm); the other reads a dimension nothing bounds (unmeasured). Without the basis a surface would render both identically, which is precisely how a manufactured zero and an honest one become indistinguishable.

knapsack_cases.name: ★★_it_is_a_REAL_knapsack_and_not_a_sort_dressed_up
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ The case that tells the two apart: greedy-by-score takes the 0.90 item and stops at a total of 0.90; the DP takes the 0.60 + 0.55 pair for 1.15. A sort-and-take-N would fail this, and it is the difference between an attention budget that is spent well and one that merely looks ranked.
knapsack_cases.expect: the pair selected, the big one excluded

knapsack_cases.name: ★_the_selection_is_OPTIMAL_against_brute_force
knapsack_cases.why: ★ Optimality asserted rather than trusted: every feasible subset of five items is enumerated and the DP's total is checked equal to the best. *Every selected widget provably outscored what it displaced* is the whole justification for a person trusting the surface, so it is worth proving over the algorithm rather than over one example.

knapsack_cases.name: every_exclusion_comes_back_with_its_score
knapsack_cases.why: The *'N other things stayed quiet'* disclosure needs something true to say. An exclusion nobody can inspect is indistinguishable from a widget that was never considered — the same OPV-29 discipline that makes the Pareto frontier report what collapsing hid.
knapsack_cases.expect: the excluded candidate carries its score

knapsack_cases.name: ★★_a_zero_score_widget_is_not_shown_and_says_so_from_the_excluded_list
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ Found by testing rather than design, and kept. The DP takes an item only when it **strictly improves** the total, so a widget scoring exactly 0 never enters the selection. That is right — `K ≈ 4` is scarce and a card worth nothing is the noise a curated surface exists to remove — and it is **at parity** with the reference, whose `dp[c-w] + v > dp[c]` behaves identically. Nothing is hidden: it was considered, it is in `excluded` with its `0.0`, and `spent` is 0.
knapsack_cases.expect: considered = 1, selected empty, excluded score 0.0, spent 0

knapsack_cases.name: an_empty_field_selects_nothing_and_says_so
knapsack_cases.why: No candidates yields two empty lists rather than an error or a fabricated placeholder — the same honest-empty treatment the surface's own design language already uses.

knapsack_cases.name: the_default_policy_is_the_articles_declared_preference
knapsack_cases.why: The article's weights survive as the default a household inherits — named in the constant's docstring as **the article's declared preference, not a derived value**. The defect was never that a default existed; it was that there was no way to hold a different one.

knapsack_cases.name: ★_a_household_may_argue_the_ratio
knapsack_cases.why: ★ The point of the row: weighting urgency harder is now something a household can *do*, not something someone edits a module constant to change. A purely-urgent widget scores higher under a stricter policy than under the default, on identical state.
knapsack_cases.expect: the stricter policy raises the score

knapsack_cases.name: ★★★_urgency_cannot_be_argued_into_SECOND_PLACE
knapsack_cases.why: ★★★ The one thing that is not arguable, refused at construction. A policy where relevance meets or beats urgency would let a **search query outrank the household being in danger** — reintroducing at the weights exactly the gaming UI-1 closed at the inputs. Both the inverted case and the **tie** are refused, because *equal* is already a surface where a query can win.

knapsack_cases.name: the_weights_must_sum_to_one_so_a_score_means_the_same_thing_everywhere
knapsack_cases.why: Keeps the score on `[0,1]`, so it is comparable across sustains and the DP's integer scaling stays interpretable. A non-finite weight is refused too — the same absent-rather-than-defaulted discipline `Fraction::of` follows.

knapsack_cases.name: ★★_a_widget_cannot_set_the_weights
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ The policy is a parameter of the **household's** view: `WidgetDecl` has nowhere to put one and `compose_view` never reads one off the set. Asserted as the observable consequence — changing the policy changes the score and leaves the **urgency itself untouched**, so the un-gameable signal stays exactly as un-gameable as UI-1 made it.

read_only_cases.name: ★_compose_changes_nothing
read_only_cases.why: ★ Read-only **by signature** — shared references in, a `View` out, and no `Registry`, so there is nothing here that could run an operator. Asserted anyway across two calls, because a signature-only guarantee is worth exactly one refactor; the same doubled discipline EVT-15 applies to replay's effect suppression.
read_only_cases.expect: state and log byte-identical after two composes

read_only_cases.name: composing_twice_gives_the_same_view
read_only_cases.why: Resolved fresh on every call and **never stored**, so two calls on unchanged inputs must agree exactly — which also means candidate ordering is deterministic and the DP's tie-breaking is reproducible rather than incidental.

read_only_cases.name: relevance_is_neutral_with_no_query_and_real_with_one
read_only_cases.why: 0.5 with no query — the common case, since the usual question is *what needs me right now* rather than a search — and a real overlap fraction when there is one. The unrelated-query case doubles as the zero-score case above, which is how that behaviour was found.
